q.passage: SENSIBLE SENTENCES? (From Week 12) Choose the word that makes sense in each of the sentences below. 1.The senator went into a lengthy (diatribe, r___________) about government waste in the military budget. 2.Most reformers are seeking to create a (schism, utopia). 3.Lorraine was criticized sharply for the (ostentatious, nominal) way in which she furnished her apartment. 4.Anyone so (ilk, timorous) should not have been selected to guard the castle. 5.My brother was promoted to a (prestigious, flamboyant) job in his company. 6.Although his speech was (anathema, jaunty) we were able to sense its underlying seriousness. 7.The failing grade was (expunged, truncated) from her record when she submitted the excellent term paper. 8.I got my job as a result of a (fractious, fortuitous) meeting with the director of personnel. 9.The bookkeeper is such an (integral, incoherent) part of our organization that we pay her a very high salary. 10.We marched in front of the embassy with (placards, inhibitions) held high. 11.Don’t (save face, wash your dirty linen in public) if you plan to run for office.
q.explanation:
[모범답안] remuneration — 문단의 논지상 이 자리에는 'remuneration'가 유일하게 자연스럽다.

q.instruction: 주어진 글 다음에 이어질 글의 순서로 가장 적절한 것은?
q.passage:
In those first words, readers want to see characters not just in the whole subjects of verbs, as government is implied in governmental, but as their simple subjects.

(A) Skim the passage for actions involving those characters, particularly actions buried in nominalizations. Ask Who is doing what? governmental intervention S ✓ government intervenes distortion S ✓ [government] distorts market evolution S ✓ markets evolve interference S ✓ [government] interferes development S ✓ [market] develops To revise, reassemble those new subjects and verbs into a ­sentence, using conjunctions such as if, although, because, when, how, and why: ✓ When a government intervenes in fast-changing technologies, it distorts how markets evolve and interferes with their ability to develop new products.

(B) In that example, ­however, they aren’t. Find the main characters.

(C) They may be possessive pronouns attached to nominalizations, objects of prepositions (particularly by and of), or only implied. In that sentence, one main character is in the adjective governmental; the other, market, is in the object of a preposition: of market evolution.
q.explanation:
원문 전개 순서는 (B) - (C) - (A)이다. 각 단락의 지시어·연결어가 앞 내용을 받아 이 순서로만 논리가 이어진다.
【출제의도】 응집 장치(지시어·연결어·정관사)로 글의 논리 순서를 재구성하는 능력을 평가한다.

q.passage:
① REVIEW WORDS DEFINITIONS 1.
② trembling, shaking with old age 2.
③ infirm, weak as a result of old age 5.
④ Knowing one synonym is good, but you will reap greater benefits from knowing several.
⑤ Below is the matching review for this week.
⑥ bursting out 4.
⑦ WEEK 25 DAY 5 REVIEW Week by week your word-power is being built.
⑧ It’s like putting money in the bank.
⑨ Remember, in our language there may be many synonyms and related meanings for each word.
q.explanation:
정답 배열은 ⑦-⑧-⑨-④-⑤-①-②-⑥-③. 흐름: ⑦ → ⑧(It) → ⑨ → ④ → ⑤ → ① → ② → ⑥ → ③ — 문두 연결어·지시어가 바로 앞 문장을 받아 이 순서로만 논리가 이어진다.
